newsitem.title: CHINA: Upturn seen in China property market.
newsitem.headline: Upturn seen in China property market.

text.p: A new wave of investment is likely to lift China's troubled property market out of a three-year slump, the official Xinhua news agency quoted a leading property specialist as saying.

Two interest rate cuts this year by the central bank would spur the market by pushing people to spend their savings, it quoted China Land Society executive director Lin Zengjie as saying in a report late on Tuesday.
But there would be no repeat of the 1992 property boom, however, because local investors had become mature and more cautious, Lin said.

Chinese officials have called for deep cuts in housing prices to revitalise the property market, which slumped after a flood of high-priced developments hit a market already limited by Beijing's anti-inflation policies.
The high cost of purchasing land and high charges by local administrative departments were the main factors keeping housing prices beyond the reach of most Chinese consumers, Lin said.

The State Planning Commission's demand that local governments cut adminstrative charges on telecommunications, roads and water and power supplies was a positive step that could cut costs to home buyers, he said.

Many urban Chinese, most of whom enjoy highly subsidised rents for their employer-owned homes, say they cannot afford to buy even the cheapest accommodation on the private market. Lin said China was not yet ready for the widespread use of mortgage loans to allow home-buyers long-term credit. He said this was because of the high interest rates on such loans and the lack of policies and supporting funds from the government.
The central bank recently banned commercial banks making home and auto loans, saying these credits were undesirable.
